conflicts.description: The same broad audiovisual-work concept is named title in IMDb and film in Sakila, with different identifier names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both under the work entity with snake_case work terminology and source-scoped work identifiers.

conflicts.description: IMDb represents a credited person name as primaryname, while Sakila calls the entity actor and separates first and last names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the entity as person while retaining display_name separately from atomic given_name and family_name.

conflicts.description: IMDb uses genre terminology while Sakila uses category for a comparable film classification concept.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the concept as genre and preserved source category identifiers as genre identifiers.

conflicts.description: The source term inventory identifies an individual physical copy rather than an aggregate stock measure.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the target entity and key to inventory_item and inventory_item_id.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are declared as number even though their descriptions define string identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Typed all IMDb identifiers as string in the target.

conflicts.description: IMDb primarytitle is declared integer but described as title text.
conflicts.resolution: Typed primary_title as string.

conflicts.description: Calendar years are represented as strings in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Typed year attributes as integer, treating source null markers as null values.

conflicts.description: Numeric durations and monetary values are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed durations as integer quantities and monetary values as number.

conflicts.description: Logical active flags are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed active-state fields as boolean.

conflicts.description: Fields described as containing date and time are declared as date.
conflicts.resolution: Typed event and update timestamps as datetime.

conflicts.description: Runtime is represented in minutes in both sources, which is not the selected standard SI duration unit.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized runtime as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is represented in days.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the rental period as seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb average rating is a numeric user score, whereas Sakila rating is a categorical audience classification.
conflicts.resolution: Kept these as separate average_rating and content_rating attributes rather than conflating their scales.

conflicts.description: Primary/display titles and original-language titles have distinct semantics despite all being title text.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped display titles to primary_title and retained original_title as a separate attribute.

conflicts.description: Current release language, original work language, and alternate-title language play different semantic roles.
conflicts.resolution: Retained distinct foreign-key roles on work and alternate_title while sharing a normalized language entity.

conflicts.description: Monetary values lack an explicit source currency.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved numeric amounts without inventing a currency code and documented reliance on the source system currency.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns encode arrays or multi-value attributes inside strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized each multi-value attribute into child or bridge resources with atomic values and explicit foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates searchable film text in film_text while core film attributes reside in film.
conflicts.resolution: Merged duplicate title and description attributes into work with provenance from both tables.

conflicts.description: IMDb models title metadata only, while Sakila separates catalog works, physical copies, and rental transactions.
conflicts.resolution: Retained normalized work, inventory_item, and rental entities so catalog identity is not conflated with physical-copy or transaction identity.

conflicts.description: The address location is an opaque geometry value whose internal geometry kind and components are unspecified.
conflicts.resolution: Retained it as a single serialized geometry field rather than inventing latitude/longitude semantics not supplied by the source.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to several genres per title, whereas Sakila expresses film categories through a many-to-many bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized both as the many-to-many work_genre relationship.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds multiple directors and writers in one crew row, while Sakila uses rows in a film-actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Exploded IMDb arrays into work_director and work_writer bridges and represented principal/cast associations in work_credit.

conflicts.description: A person can be known for several works and a work can be associated with several persons.
conflicts.resolution: Created the many-to-many person_known_work bridge.

conflicts.description: Episodes and series are both titles linked by a recursive one-to-many relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Created episode as a relationship resource with separate episode and parent-series foreign keys to work.

conflicts.description: One catalog film can have many physical inventory copies.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved work-to-inventory_item as a one-to-many relationship.

conflicts.description: Equivalent work entities use incompatible natural-looking alphanumeric and surrogate identifiers, and film_text omits an explicit key declaration.
conflicts.resolution: Defined source-scoped string work_id as the unified key and included all corresponding source identifiers in its provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent credited-person entities use different identifier systems.
conflicts.resolution: Defined a source-scoped string person_id with both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: IMDb alternate titles have no declared primary key although ordering is unique only within a title.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic alternate_title_id and retained ordering as a non-identity sequence attribute.

conflicts.description: Credit rows have no common declared key; IMDb uses per-title ordering while Sakila identifies associations through foreign-key pairs.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic credit_id so source-specific sequence and relationship keys remain semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Sakila provides a payment identifier described as a surrogate key but does not declare a table primary key.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted payment_id to the target payment primary key.

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare no primary keys despite representing unique entity associations.
conflicts.resolution: Used the corresponding foreign-key pairs as composite target keys where the association has no additional row identity.
